title: Beginning anew and leaving familiar words
meaning: You can freely try another way of promising and still feel sadness about a familiar phrase you no longer want to repeat.
text: An unexpected conversational turn sometimes changes your relationship with familiar words. The Hermit in the physical position of your Vishuddha helps explain something understood through reflection. The Fool in energy encourages you to begin differently and try a form of answer that is not yet settled. Death in emotions brings farewell to a familiar phrase. A free beginning need not remove sadness: you can want to speak differently while feeling that the old words held an important place between you.

For example, you discuss the promise “We will never argue”. An unexpected “Could we promise to listen even during a disagreement?” opens another direction. You explain why this thought feels more honest and decide to leave the earlier formula behind. **New words can bring pleasure and sadness together**. Conversation gains freedom to seek a living promise rather than a flawless picture of communication. Yet leaving the beautiful phrase can feel like a small farewell to how you imagined the conversation about closeness itself.

It becomes harder if a considered explanation turns into proof that the earlier words were naive. A new beginning then demands devaluing something that once brought warmth. The Fool’s constructive openness helps you try another form without passing that verdict on the old one. You can acknowledge the former wish’s value without repeating an unsuitable promise. Sadness concerns the words left behind rather than predicting the outcome of your relationship.
